title: Chernobyl Prayer

vibeProfile.oneLine: The voices of those who survived Chernobyl, gathered into a requiem.

summary: Svetlana Alexievich gathered the voices of those who lived through the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster: the widows of firefighters, evacuated villagers, scientists, soldiers and children, each testifying to a catastrophe unlike any before it. Out of their monologues she builds a devastating oral history of loss, courage and a poisoned world. The Nobel laureate's method turns raw human testimony into literature, and this may be her most harrowing and unforgettable book, a requiem for a place and a way of life.
whyReadIt: Alexievich's harrowing chorus of Chernobyl survivors, turning raw testimony into literature. A requiem you won't forget.
awards: Part of the work honoured by the Nobel Prize in Literature 2015

funFacts.text: Alexievich won the 2015 Nobel Prize for the documentary method this book exemplifies.
